name: Pelatiah
overview: Pelatiah is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezekiel, identified uniquely as the son of Benaiah. The biblical text does not provide information about his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His mention is brief, focusing primarily on his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Pelatiah means 'y-h-v-h rescues,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning connected to the Lord's deliverance. This proper name appears in Ezekiel 11:1 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Pelatiah as the son of Benaiah. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pelatiah's significance in Scripture is tied to his identification as the son of Benaiah in Ezekiel 11:1. While the text does not elaborate on his actions or role, his mention contributes to the historical and genealogical context within the prophetic narrative. This brief reference situates him within the broader framework of God's dealings with His people as recorded by the prophet Ezekiel.
